citeAs: Pratap, Vineel, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, and Ronan Collobert. (2020). MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. Preprint.
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
description: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) is a large-scale multilingual read-speech dataset derived from LibriVox audiobooks and corresponding text sources. It covers 8 languages and includes 44.5K hours of English plus about 6K hours for the other languages, with released language models and baseline ASR resources.
name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports human verification of development and test transcripts and measures WER between generated transcripts and human-rated transcripts for each language. It also reports test accuracy of the gender classifier used for speaker gender labeling, including 95% on LibriSpeech development/test speakers and manual checks of 96% on Dutch and 94% on Polish.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels were created by generating pseudo-labels for audio segments with acoustic models and 4-gram language models, retrieving matching transcript spans from source book texts using TF-IDF and Smith-Waterman alignment, filtering candidate transcripts whose WER against pseudo-labels exceeded 40%, and performing human verification on development and test transcripts where transcribers corrected only clear and obvious errors.
rai:dataBiases: To avoid potential bias from human transcribing, the authors asked transcribers to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors. The dataset is limited to read audiobooks from LibriVox and selected languages with sufficient audiobook hours and available text sources, which may bias coverage toward those languages and source materials.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by downloading LibriVox audiobooks in eight selected languages, downloading or manually finding the corresponding text sources, segmenting long audiobook audio into 10–20 second clips, generating pseudo-labels with acoustic models and language models, and retrieving original transcripts by matching pseudo-labels to source texts.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some audiobooks were excluded because corresponding text sources could not be downloaded, links were invalid or redirected incorrectly, candidate labels were filtered during transcript retrieval, or books had corrupted metadata such as missing title or speaker/author information.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of LibriVox read-audiobook audio and corresponding source book texts from websites such as Project Gutenberg, archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, and other language-specific online text sources.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset covers only 8 languages selected based on available audiobook hours and text-source availability, and the final training data is smaller than available audiobook totals because some text sources could not be downloaded and some candidates were filtered. The paper also notes that number replacement using pseudo-label alignment is not perfect because pseudo-labels may not always be correct.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Long audio files were segmented into 10–20 second clips using silence-based splitting guided by acoustic-model timestamps. The dataset was split into train/dev/test with no speaker overlap, balanced gender and duration in dev/test, truncation of high-duration speakers, and additional limited-supervision subsets of 10 hours, 1 hour, and six 10-minute sets per language.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz and segmented into 10–20 second utterances. Text was normalized with NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters such as punctuation, subscripts/superscripts, emojis, and escape symbols, removal of end-of-line hyphenation, and filtering to valid unicode characters for each language orthography.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for speech research, especially automatic speech recognition (ASR), multilingual ASR, low-resource training benchmarks, and text-to-speech (TTS) research.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Time-Depth Separable convolution acoustic models with ASG loss, wav2letter@anywhere for streaming inference, beam-search decoding with 4-gram language models, TF-IDF similarity scoring, Smith-Waterman alignment, pdftotext for extracting book text, KenLM for language models, and an SVM gender classifier with RBF kernel for speaker gender labeling.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker gender labels were assigned using a classifier for dataset splitting, and the in-house data used to train segmentation models is described as completely de-identified.
